_comment_split: SPLIT from the monolithic S10.json (2026-08-30, ralph/T2-S10-COST). The original single S10 step-script asks for 439,336 planned frames; measured in-play at 0.097 s/frame (right after a real combat exchange) that prices the segment's own remainder at 40,195 s against a 14,400 s per-segment ceiling -- see ralph/reports/gate-f-run-20260828T183531Z/S10/BLOCKER.md. The dominant cost is NOT combat: the S10-89..S10-106 post-win walk-back alone is 378,750 of those 439,336 planned frames (86%), because it retraces roughly 7.6 km of the whole Meadows on foot per section 0.6's no-shortcut rule. S10 is split into five sub-segments chained by save handoff exactly like S01-S09, each individually costed comfortably under the ceiling: S10a (this file, Hall entry -> gauntlet -> recovery -> elite), S10b (Warden -> legendary -> release ceremony), S10c/S10d/S10e (the walk-back, cut at the same landmarks S05-S09's own segment boundaries already use -- Old Mill Crossing and South Bridge -- so the return trip's cuts mirror the outbound journey's). See ralph/reports/handover-T2-S10-COST-2026-08-30.md for the full frame-budget analysis and the reprice mechanics (operator_harness.gd's _apply_price) that motivated exactly this split.

steps.title: how this segment is entered

args.text: This is the FIRST of S10's five split sub-segments (S10a..S10e; see this file's header). Its entry save is `S09-exit`, unchanged from the original monolithic S10 -- the split adds new handoff points AFTER this one, it does not move the chapter's real entry. The three steps below are the handoff's own mechanics: the live save directory is emptied first so the title's Load list has exactly one non-empty slot and auto-focuses it (`title_screen.gd` focuses the FIRST non-empty slot), then slot 4 is seeded from the run directory, then the load is driven through the production title-screen Load path by synthetic input.
